title: 45-Day Identification Strategy
name: 45-Day Identification Strategy
metaTitle: 45-Day Identification Strategy in Fort Worth, TX
metaDescription: Fort Worth 1031 exchange 45-day identification strategy: sourcing and documenting replacement candidates across Alliance, downtown, and Southlake before the deadline.

sections.html: The 45-day identification period begins on the closing date of the relinquished property and cannot be extended for any reason, including a pending contract that has not yet been signed. Fort Worth investors exchanging out of a downtown office condo or a Near Southside multifamily building need a sourcing plan in place before that clock starts, not after.

sections.heading: Pre-Closing Preparation
sections.html:
Because 45 days is short relative to typical commercial due diligence, the identification strategy is built before the relinquished sale closes, using the weeks of marketing and contract negotiation to pre-screen candidates. Broker relationships covering Alliance industrial, Cultural District retail, and Southlake office product are engaged early so a workable list exists on day one rather than day thirty.

Pre-closing preparation also means confirming with the qualified intermediary how identification notices will be delivered and time-stamped, since a late notice has no cure.

sections.heading: Structuring the Written Identification
sections.html:
Identification must be unambiguous: a street address or legal description, delivered in writing, signed, and sent to the qualified intermediary or another party involved in the exchange before midnight on day 45. A verbal mention to a broker or an email describing a submarket generally, without a specific parcel, does not satisfy the requirement.

  • Confirm the exact street address or legal description for each candidate
  • Choose the three-property, 200%, or 95% rule before drafting the notice
  • Deliver the signed notice to the qualified intermediary in writing
  • Retain a delivery record showing the date and time sent

sections.heading: Managing Multiple Submarkets at Once
sections.html: Investors identifying across more than one Fort Worth-area submarket, for example an Alliance distribution building alongside a Grapevine retail pad, benefit from tracking each candidate's due diligence status separately, since financing timelines and seller responsiveness rarely move at the same pace across corridors.

sections.heading: Revising an Identification Before Day 45
sections.html: An identification notice can be revoked or replaced any number of times before the 45th day, which allows a candidate that falls out of contract to be swapped for another without penalty. After the deadline passes, the list is locked, so the last version delivered in writing is the one that governs the exchange.

sections.heading: Building a Realistic Timeline Around Fort Worth Deal Flow
sections.html:
Commercial listings in Fort Worth-area submarkets move at different speeds depending on asset type and season, and a 45-day window that feels comfortable for a downtown office trade can feel tight for an Alliance industrial search during a period of heavy leasing activity. Mapping out a week-by-week plan, brokerage outreach in the first week, tours in the second, letters of intent by the third, gives the identification team enough runway to negotiate rather than settle for whatever candidate happens to be available on day forty.

That timeline also has to account for seller responsiveness, since a property owner in Southlake or Grapevine unaccustomed to a compressed exchange deadline may not move at the pace an investor needs. Flagging the exchange timeline early in negotiations, rather than after a letter of intent is already signed, helps set seller expectations correctly from the start.

A weekly status check against the plan, rather than a single review at the outset, catches slippage while there is still time to react. If broker outreach in an Alliance-area search stalls in week one, that gap is easier to close by expanding the search to Haslet or Saginaw in week two than it is to discover on day forty that the candidate pool never materialized. The same discipline applies to a downtown office search, where a slower-than-expected response from ownership groups near Sundance Square can be addressed early by widening outreach rather than waiting and hoping activity picks up. A brief written status note after each weekly check, even a few lines summarizing what moved and what did not, gives the team a record to reference if the search needs to change direction later in the window. By the final week before the deadline, the plan typically narrows from a broad candidate search down to a short list ready for the written notice, with any remaining uncertainty resolved rather than carried into the identification document itself.

faqs.q: Can the 45-day window be extended for a Fort Worth investor waiting on a lender commitment?
faqs.a: No. The 45-day identification period is fixed by statute and does not extend for financing delays, weather, or any other circumstance affecting the taxpayer.

faqs.q: Does an identification notice need to name a specific building or just a submarket?
faqs.a: A specific address or legal description is required. Naming a general area such as Alliance or the Cultural District without a parcel-level identifier does not meet the standard.

faqs.q: Who should receive the written identification notice?
faqs.a: The qualified intermediary is the most common recipient, though the rules also permit delivery to certain other parties to the exchange. Investors should confirm the correct recipient with their qualified intermediary before the deadline.

faqs.q: Can an investor identify a property they have not yet put under contract?
faqs.a: Yes. Identification only requires a specific description of the property, not an executed purchase contract, though most investors move quickly to contract given the following closing deadline.

faqs.q: What happens if no valid identification is delivered by day 45?
faqs.a: The exchange fails and the transaction is treated as a taxable sale. There is no extension or cure period once the 45th day passes without a compliant written notice.
